evals.prompt: The bug-fix design and scope are approved. Implement the change in small units, run the focused test and relevant regression checks, and report what remains unverified.
Implement the approved README and editor-configuration changes. Use the available Markdown and JSON validation rather than inventing a product test, then report the checks you ran.
The review findings have been triaged. Apply only the accepted fixes, run the relevant checks, and hand off the resulting evidence.
The review findings are triaged. Implement only authorized Act now items, leave Defer and No action unchanged, run relevant checks, and return actual reviewer context.
I think onboarding needs improvement, but the affected users, desired behavior, scope, and acceptance criteria are not defined. Help me clarify the request.
Before touching code, design the change scope, affected consumers, risks, stop conditions, and verification coverage.
Review this existing diff for correctness, safety, maintainability, performance, and missing tests. Do not edit it.
The fix is already complete. Independently verify the diff and test results, separate confirmed from unconfirmed items, and assess the remaining risk without making changes.

Prepare this authentication change for execution, but do not edit until its exact action, scope, safety controls, recovery treatment, residual risk, and execution authority are decision-ready. Assess what is missing.
Two materially identical implementation attempts failed under the same hypothesis. Stop editing, organize confirmed facts and unknowns, and select one structurally different next check.
